concepts.def: Money earned from sales (price x quantity)
Cost that doesn't change with output (e.g. rent)
Cost that rises with output (e.g. materials)
Gross profit minus all other expenses

walkthroughs.body_html:
Revenue = price × quantity sold.

It's the top line on the income statement — money in, before any costs are taken off.

Fixed costs stay the same whatever the output (rent, salaries, insurance).

Variable costs change with output (raw materials, packaging, piece-rate wages). Total cost = fixed + variable.

Gross profit = revenue − cost of sales. It shows how well the core product makes money.

Net profit = gross profit − all other expenses (rent, wages, marketing). The true bottom line.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between fixed and variable costs?
options: Fixed costs do not change with output level (e.g. rent, salaries); variable costs change in proportion to output (e.g. raw materials, hourly wages).
Fixed costs are paid every month and variable costs are paid weekly.
Gross profit is profit before VAT and net profit is profit after VAT.
Fixed costs are the cheapest costs and variable costs are the most expensive.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between gross profit and net profit?
options: Gross profit is profit before VAT and net profit is profit after VAT.
Profit is what businesses earn; revenue is what employees earn.
Gross profit and net profit are the same thing.
Gross profit = revenue minus cost of goods sold (direct costs only); net profit = revenue minus ALL costs including overheads, interest and tax. Net profit is the bottom line.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between profit and revenue?
options: Revenue is total income from sales (price x quantity sold); profit is revenue minus total costs — what is left after paying for everything.
Gross profit is profit before VAT and net profit is profit after VAT.
Profit and revenue are different words for the same thing.
Profit is what businesses earn; revenue is what employees earn.
